items.title: The Chow group in dimension k is the image of the K-group of sheaves supported in dimension at most k inside the K-group of sheaves supported in dimensions k+1 and k
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the map CH_k(X) -> K_0(Coh_{<= k+1}(X)/Coh_{<= k-1}(X)) induced by the from-Chow-to-K construction is a bijection onto the image B_k(X) of the natural map from K_0(Coh_{<= k}(X)/Coh_{<= k-1}(X)) (statement lines 18508-18524). The proof translates rational equivalence into K-theory: it identifies Z_k(X) with K_0 of the quotient category of sheaves supported in dimension at most k compatibly with the map, then takes an element [A] - [B] representing a class that dies in the larger quotient, and unwinds that vanishing through the two parts of the Serre subcategory K-group lemma to produce sheaves A', B' supported in dimension at most k-1 such that [A + A'] - [B + B'] is zero in K_0(Coh_{k+1}(X)), and then a (2, 1)-periodic complex (F, phi, psi) in Coh_{<= k+1}(X) whose H^0 and H^1 are A + A' and B + B' (proof lines 18526-18553). The cycle-theoretic input is then the preceding lemma comparing the k-cycles of the two cohomology sheaves, which yields [A + A']_k ~ rat [B + B']_k and hence that [A] - [B] is rationally equivalent to zero (proof lines 18554-18568). The unwinding of the K-theoretic vanishing into an actual periodic complex is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
